title: A closed subscheme covered by effective Cartier divisors and a codimension two closed subset is, away from codimension two, an effective Cartier divisor supported on it

standard_prerequisites.name: An integral effective Cartier divisor has a discrete valuation ring at its generic point, and one can speak of the valuation of an element of the stalk of an ideal sheaf there
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited in the same chapter at proof lines 3104-3106
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the local rings whose valuations define the multiplicities a_i.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local equation of an effective Cartier divisor at a point of the divisor, so that the divisors D_i through a point are cut out by prime elements of the local ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the prime elements f_i in terms of which the product of the f_i to the a_i is formed.

standard_prerequisites.name: A regular local ring is a unique factorisation domain, cited from the chapter on more algebra, and the same-chapter statement that irreducible codimension one components of a closed subscheme in a UFD situation are effective Cartier divisors
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the existence part of the final sentence: a regular or locally UFD ambient produces the required divisors D_i.

core_obligations: Define the multiplicities: let xi_i be the generic point of D_i and O_i the local ring there, a discrete valuation ring, and let a_i be the minimal valuation at xi_i of an element of the stalk of the ideal sheaf of Z; observe that a_i is positive only for the finitely many divisors that occur as irreducible components of Z (proof lines 3102-3109).

Reduce to a point: for a point x with local ring A, let D_1 to D_n be the finitely many divisors with x in D_i and a_i positive, and choose local equations f_i in A, which are prime elements with O_i the localisation of A at f_i; write I for the stalk of the ideal sheaf of Z and record that after localising at f_i the ideal I becomes the principal ideal generated by f_i to the a_i (proof lines 3111-3120).

Prove the key claim that I is contained in the principal ideal generated by the product of the f_i to the a_i, by showing that the localisation map from A modulo the i-th power of f_i into the localisation at f_i modulo that same power is injective, and then peeling off one prime element at a time using that the f_i are pairwise distinct and hence become units at the other localisations (proof lines 3122-3143).

Read off the two conclusions: the containment of ideal sheaves says that D is contained in Z, and the equality of the two divisors at each generic point xi_i says that D to Z is an isomorphism away from codimension two in X (proof lines 3145-3149).

Prove the final existence sentence: since a regular local ring is a UFD it suffices to treat the UFD case, where the codimension one irreducible components of Z can be taken as the D_i, each of them being an effective Cartier divisor by the same-chapter statement invoked (proof lines 3147-3153).
proof_roadmap: Define the multiplicities a_i as minimal valuations at the generic points of the divisors and prove that they vanish for all but finitely many indices (proof lines 3102-3109).

Work at a point and prove that the stalk of the ideal sheaf of Z is contained in the principal ideal cut out by the product of the local equations of the relevant divisors, by an induction peeling off the prime elements (proof lines 3111-3143).

Translate the containment back into the containment of divisors, get the isomorphism away from codimension two from the agreement at the generic points, and handle the existence sentence through the UFD case (proof lines 3145-3153).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a closed subscheme Z of a Noetherian scheme is covered by integral effective Cartier divisors D_i together with a closed subset all of whose components have codimension at least two, then a nonnegative combination of the D_i is an effective Cartier divisor contained in Z and isomorphic to Z away from codimension two (statement lines 3075-3100). The counted proof is a genuine local argument: it defines the multiplicities a_i as valuations at the discrete valuation rings of the generic points, shows all but finitely many vanish, and then at an arbitrary point proves the delicate claim that the stalk of the ideal sheaf of Z is contained in the principal ideal generated by the product of the local equations of the relevant divisors, by an induction that peels off prime elements one at a time using that they are pairwise distinct (proof lines 3102-3143). It is H2: the arguments are carried out in full in the counted span and the only cited inputs are the discrete valuation ring property, local equations of Cartier divisors, and the UFD case used for the final existence sentence.
